actions.body: The literature on adaptive planning (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da) and sunk cost effects (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca) provides a foundation for evaluating research agendas. Our synthesis confirms that intelligence often overvalues persistence in the face of negative feedback. By comparing the cost of current inquiry with potential gains found in adjacent domains (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb), we identify a threshold where abandonment becomes the rational, utility-maximizing action. This notebook formalizes the transition from persistent effort to calculated termination.
actions.lede: Do intelligences recognize the 'sunk cost' in their own inquiries? This synthesis examines the formal rational criteria for abandoning a research agenda when epistemic returns diminish.
